claims.text: Multiple uniprot_variants records with score 1 link NOD2 variants (e.g. rs2066844, rs2066845, rs104895439) to inflammatory bowel disease 1 (MONDO_0009960, a descendant of the selected IBD term MONDO_0005265), supported by literature spanning 2001–2024. These are descendant-of-selected records, not direct evidence for MONDO_0005265.

EVA records report multiple NOD2 variants annotated to Crohn disease (MONDO_0005011, a descendant of IBD), including high-scoring (0.92) loss-of-function variants such as rs2066845 (RCV002512782) and rs2066844 (RCV002512783) classified with risk direction. These are indirect evidence for MONDO_0005265.

GWAS credible set records provide direct genetic association evidence for NOD2 with IBD (MONDO_0005265), with scores ranging from ~0.32 to ~0.93 across multiple published studies, including PMID 28067908, 37156999, and 37965154.

Gene burden analysis records (source: gene_burden, direct disease: MONDO_0005265 and MONDO_0005011) associate NOD2 LoF variants with risk for inflammatory bowel disease and Crohn disease, with odds ratios in the range of ~1.6–2.9 (PMID 34375979, AZ PheWAS). The IBD-direct record (MONDO_0005265) has a score of 0.35; Crohn records are descendant-of-selected.

The uniprot_literature record for NOD2 (MONDO_0009960, descendant) with score 1 cites twelve publications including PMIDs 11385576, 11385577, 12514169, 15044951, 15998797, and 27812135, supporting NOD2 genetic literature association with IBD-1 (a descendant of the selected IBD term).

The Open Targets function annotation describes NOD2 as a pattern recognition receptor (PRR) that senses muramyl dipeptide (MDP) from bacterial peptidoglycan, activates NF-κB and MAP kinase signaling via RIPK2, and plays a role in gastrointestinal immunity and intestinal microbiota balance. This is a target-level annotation not specific to IBD.

Tractability records indicate NOD2 has an approved small molecule (SM modality, label 'Approved Drug', value true) and a high-quality ligand (SM, value true) at the target level. These are target-level annotations and do not establish approval for IBD or any specific indication.

The safety section returned zero curated records (complete_empty retrieval). This means no curated safety annotations were returned under this query; it does not establish that NOD2 is safe or that no safety concerns exist.

Animal model (IMPC) records link NOD2 LoF to multiple IBD-related descendant phenotypes including MONDO_0009960 (IBD-1), Orphanet_238569 (autosomal recessive early-onset IBD), MONDO_0033643 (IBD-30), MONDO_0012941 (IBD-25), MONDO_0054849 (IBD-29), MONDO_0005538 (proctitis), and MONDO_0030314, all with risk direction. These are indirect (descendant-of-selected) model evidence.

Evidence retrieval was truncated at 300 of 4003 total evidence rows (3-page snapshot bound). The clinical section also stopped at 300 of 4003 rows with 0 drug rows returned. Absence of drug or approval evidence cannot be concluded from this partial retrieval.
